svg.aria-label: Animated diagram of replication in a walgit cluster. A git client pushes to a primary front-end, which uploads one immutable WAL entry to the object store and advances the gitwal.pb index from ETag e1 to e2. The primary then sends a UDP gossip datagram announcing the new sequence number to a replica. When the datagram is delivered, the replica reconciles from the object store immediately, so a later fetch on the replica issues a conditional GET that returns 304 Not Modified and is served straight from the local copy. When the datagram is dropped, the replica stays stale; the fetch's conditional GET returns 200 with the new index, and the replica catches up from the object store before serving the fetch.
